# What it is

picklerick is the R binding of SCX, a format-to-format interoperability
engine for single-cell data written in Rust. SCX reads a count matrix as a
stream of cell chunks and writes it out again in another layout, so memory
is bounded by the chunk size rather than the dataset. It has no Python
dependency and links its own HDF5, so it does not interfere with `rhdf5` or
`hdf5r` in the same session.

picklerick keeps that engine behind a small R surface: one reader, one
inspector, one converter, one writer, and a DelayedArray seed.

# What it does

- **Reads** AnnData `.h5ad` files and Zarr stores, H5Seurat files, 10x HDF5
  and MatrixMarket output, and BPCells directories. The format is detected
  from the content, not the extension.
- **Builds** the R object you want from any of them: a
  `SingleCellExperiment`, a `Seurat` object, a light AnnData-like handle that
  defers the S4 cost, or the raw pieces as a list.
- **Leaves the matrix on disk** when asked, as a `DelayedMatrix` that reads
  only the cells a block touches.
- **Converts** file to file, streamed, to `.h5ad`, `.h5seurat` or an AnnData
  Zarr v3 store.
- **Writes** a `SingleCellExperiment` back to `.h5ad`.

```{r}
library(picklerick)

inspect("atlas.h5ad")                        # metadata only
sce <- read_h5ad("atlas.h5ad")               # SingleCellExperiment
obj <- read_h5ad("atlas.h5ad", as = "Seurat")
sce <- read_zarr("atlas.zarr", lazy = TRUE)  # matrix stays on disk
convert("atlas.h5seurat", "atlas.h5ad")
write_h5ad(sce, "out.h5ad")
```

The vignette *Reading single-cell files with picklerick*
(`vignette("picklerick")`) runs every one of these on a dataset shipped with
the package.

Reference pages are being generated from the roxygen sources; until then
the help topics below are marked TODO and the two vignettes are the
documentation. Progress is tracked in
[scx issue #88](https://github.com/btraven00/scx/issues/88).

| Function | Does | Help page |
|---|---|---|
| `read_h5ad(path, as, lazy, ...)` | Read any supported file into a `SingleCellExperiment` (default), `Seurat`, AnnData handle or list | TODO |
| `read_zarr(path, ...)` | Same, named for Zarr stores | TODO |
| `inspect(path)` | Shape, column names, embedding keys and per-layer sparsity, without reading the matrix | TODO |
| `convert(input, output)` | Stream one file into another format, chosen by the output extension | TODO |
| `write_h5ad(sce, path)` | Write a `SingleCellExperiment` as `.h5ad` | TODO |
| `uns(x, key)` | Read one key of `uns` on demand | TODO |
| `as_sce(x)`, `as_seurat(x)` | Turn the AnnData handle from `as = "AnnData"` into an S4 object | TODO |
| `PicklerickMatrix(path, layer)` | A `DelayedMatrix` whose blocks are read through SCX | TODO |
| `PicklerickMatrixSeed` | The seed class behind it, with `dim`, `dimnames`, `extract_array`, `extract_sparse_array`, `chunkdim` | TODO |

# Where it fits

For plain `.h5ad` files Bioconductor already has `zellkonverter` (through
Python) and `HDF5Array::H5SparseMatrix` (lazy). picklerick is for the cases
those do not cover: no Python available, Zarr stores, H5Seurat, 10x and
BPCells inputs, one reader for all of them, and lazy access to the non-HDF5
ones.
